reports.title: System of National Accounts (ESA 2010)
reports.description: Ukrainian national accounts compiled in line with ESA 2010; candidate status granted 2022.

release_schedule.note: SSSU (Держстат) does not publish a dated advance release calendar for national accounts specifically (the general stat.gov.ua/en/releases calendar and the 2026 primary-statistics calendar at km.ukrstat.gov.ua/ukr/statinf/kalendar26.htm do not list national accounts as a separate scheduled item -- it was dropped from that calendar's active topic list). Instead, timing was inferred from actual file-publish evidence on the Quarterly National Accounts dataset page: the file for 'Consolidated national accounts for I quarter of 2026' was uploaded in the site's 2026-06 folder (i.e. released around June 2026, ~3 months after the March 31 quarter-end), and the consolidated annual national accounts for full-year 2025 was uploaded in the 2026-03 folder (~3 months after the Dec 31 year-end). Both lags are consistent with the ~T+90-day quarterly/annual transmission timelines under the EU ESA 2010 framework (Regulation (EU) No 549/2013 and amending Regulation (EU) 2023/734) that SSSU cites as the methodological basis for this statistical observation (Plan of State Statistical Observations for 2026, item 2.02). Applying that same ~3-month lag going forward gives the entries below. Ukraine also had a multi-year backlog/restoration of 2022-2025 national accounts data (completed by Dec 2025) which may still affect near-term regularity.

The national-accounts landing page (statistica.gov.md/en/national-accounts-9494.html) lists specific upcoming calendar dates for 2026: Q2 2026 GDP on 2026-09-14, Q3 2026 GDP on 2026-12-14, and final 2025 national accounts on 2026-12-29. These align with the 75-day rule and support the corpus's releases_per_year=4 for the quarterly GDP/national accounts series.

The next entry is computed from the stated t+90-days rule (Q2 2026 ends 2026-06-30, +90 days ≈ 2026-09-28) rather than read off a calendar; precision downgraded to 'month' to reflect that the exact day is approximate. _dropped.why: SETTLED 2026-08-09 (cheap-check pass): THE ERROR IS MONSTAT'S OWN, NOT A TRANSCRIPTION ARTEFACT. The primary PDF was fetched directly this session -- monstat.org/uploads/files/kvalitet/bdp/2021/Quality%20report%202021%20AGDP.pdf, 'Quality Report: Annual Gross Domestic Product 2021' -- and it prints, verbatim: "National accounts are compiled in accordance with the European System of Accounts (ESA 2010), which is published in the Official Journal of the European Commission as Annex A to Regulation (EU) No 1306/2010." Character for character what Grok transcribed, including the regulation number. Grok's transcription is vindicated; MONSTAT's document carries a wrong citation. ESA 2010 is Annex A to Regulation (EU) No 549/2013, which is what this corpus's `esa-2010` node is; there is no Regulation (EU) No 1306/2010 on national accounts (1306/2013 is CAP financing, a different subject entirely). The minted `cites` edge is UNAFFECTED and stands: MONSTAT names ESA 2010 by name and by the methodology it applies, and the edge was never built on the regulation number. Kept as a `caveat` rather than closed, because the caveat is now a finding worth carrying -- a source document in this corpus contains a demonstrated citation error, which is exactly the sort of thing Research.1.md sec.2's quote-as-found rule exists to preserve. A future session should NOT silently correct it. ORIGINAL ENTRY BELOW. MONSTAT's own quoted text cites "Regulation (EU) No 1306/2010" as the source of ESA 2010 Annex A. That regulation number does not match ESA 2010 (Regulation (EU) No 549/2013) and does not correspond to any known EU regulation on national accounts. Quoted verbatim as found rather than silently corrected, per Research.1.md §2 — but NOT verified against the primary MONSTAT document directly, only against Grok's transcription. Needs a direct check of the source PDF before this edge is treated as fully confirmed: either MONSTAT's own document contains the error, or it was introduced in transcription. [2026-08-07: reason `caveat` (annotation on the minted edge, which stands); endpoints restored when the caveat reason was added to the schema.]

Georgia, EU candidate only since late 2023. Geostat's own national accounts documentation states SNA 2008 as its basis; ESA 2010 appears only indirectly via Eurostat recommendations for revisions (HERP) and the Code of Practice, with no explicit alignment-obligation language. A clean, informative negative result — the newest candidacy has not yet produced published ESA 2010 alignment language, consistent with the pattern taking time to show up in public documentation.

_dropped.why: San Marino: no EU membership, no candidate status, included deliberately as a dead-end test (contrast to Liechtenstein, which turned out to have distinct ESA-aligned accounts despite similar size). Searches for a San Marino statistics office, national accounts, ESA/SEC 2010 returned only pre-2010 IMF GDDS references to ESA 95, an IMF note on the general inadequacy of San Marino's national accounts statistics, and a 2026 news item describing a newly created Unità Nazionale di Statistica aimed at future international alignment. No current published national-accounts series exists. The absence is real and, per the 2026 item, provisional rather than permanent — San Marino appears to be a country mid-transition toward having a statistics office at all.
